full_text_zh:
[P1] 朱莉娅·唐纳森 (英) 文  阿克塞尔·舍夫勒 (德) 图
咕噜牛
小妞妞
任溶溶 译
外语教学与研究出版社
世界经典图画书系列

[P2] 咕噜牛小妞妞
“咕噜牛爸爸警告他的小妞妞，
千万不要去密林里头，那儿有只凶恶的大老鼠会抓住你。
可是，一个风雪交加的晚上，
小妞妞踮着脚尖，溜出了家……”
风刮得猛，雪下得大，可是咕噜牛小妞妞溜出了她的家。
她带着既兴奋又期待的眼神出发了，
她想亲自去确认爸爸的话。
你想知道小妞妞是否找到了传说中那只凶恶的大老鼠吗？
建议你快跟随着小妞妞，
一同走入神秘森林中去冒险吧！
朱莉娅·唐纳森 (英) 文  阿克塞尔·舍夫勒 (德) 图
任溶溶 译

[P3] 咕噜牛爸爸警告他的小妞妞，
千万不要去密林里头。
“为什么不行？为什么不可以？”
“因为那儿有只凶恶的大老鼠会抓住你。
那个坏家伙我见过一次，
不过那是很久很久以前的事。”

“他长的什么样子？快给我讲一讲，爸爸。
他是不是非常非常凶，非常非常大？”

[P4] “我已经记不清楚了。”咕噜牛爸爸说道。
他想啊想啊想，使劲挠着后脑勺儿。

“那只凶恶的大老鼠，非常非常壮，
他有一条带鳞片的尾巴，非常非常长。

他的两只眼睛，红得像两团可怕的火，
一根一根的胡子，比铁丝还要硬得多。”

[P5] 一个风雪交加的晚上，
咕噜牛爸爸睡着了，呼噜打得震天响。
小妞妞在家里闷得慌。
她认为自己勇敢又胆大，
就踮着脚尖，溜出了家。
风刮得猛，雪下得大。
小妞妞说：“我不害怕！”
她一步一步，向密林深处走。

[P6] 瞧啊，瞧啊！雪地里有痕迹！
这是谁留下的？它会通到哪里去？
从木头堆底下，伸出一条长尾巴。
会不会就是那只大老鼠啊？

[P7] 那动物哧溜哧溜爬出来。一对眼睛小得很。
他的嘴边没胡子——胡子一根也没有。

“你不是那只大老鼠。”“我当然不是。”蛇说道，
“他这会儿准在什么地方，吃着咕噜牛蛋糕。”

风刮得猛，雪下得大。
小妞妞说：“我不害怕！”

[P8] 瞧啊，瞧啊！雪地上有足迹！
这些是谁留下的？它们会通到哪里去？
树洞里露出两只眼睛，闪闪发光亮晶晶。
会不会就是大老鼠的红眼睛？

[P9] 那动物飞下来。他的尾巴短得很。
他的嘴边也没胡子——胡子一根也没有。

“你不是那只大老鼠。”“我当然不是。”回答的是只猫头鹰，
“他这会儿准在什么地方，吃着咕噜牛肉饼。”

风刮得猛，雪下得大。
小妞妞说：“我不害怕！”

[P10] 瞧啊，瞧啊！雪地上有足迹！
这些是谁留下的？它们会通到哪里去？
终于看到了小胡子！还有一个树底下的家！
这就是那只大老鼠的家吗？

[P11] 那动物走出来。他的眼睛不像火，一点儿也不红。
他的胡子也不硬，他的尾巴毛茸茸。

“你不是那只大老鼠。”“我当然不是。”狐狸回答，
“他这会儿准在什么地方，吃着咕噜牛肉干儿喝热茶。”

小妞妞坐在积雪的树墩上。
“全是骗人！”她心里想，
“我不相信，凶恶的大老鼠真会有……”

[P12] 不过那儿有只小老鼠，刚刚走出他的家门口。
他不大，也不凶，但到底也算是老鼠。哈哈哈——
当我的夜宵，味道一定顶呱呱！

[P13] “慢着！”小老鼠说，“在你吃我之前，
我有个朋友你得见一见。
只要我跳上那棵榛子树，
就可以把他叫出来——一只凶恶的大老鼠！”

小妞妞听后松开手，
“凶恶的大老鼠——这么说来还真有！
“你就等着瞧吧。”小老鼠脱身上了树，
大声召唤那只凶恶的大老鼠。

[P14] 月亮出来了，圆又亮。
一个可怕的影子投到了雪地上。
这是什么动物啊，那么大，那么凶，又那么壮？
尾巴、胡子那么长，见了让人心发慌！
他的耳朵大又长，
肩上扛的榛子就跟巨石一个样儿！

[P15] “是那只凶恶的大老鼠！”小妞妞一边逃，一边叫。
小老鼠从树上跳下来，吱吱吱吱得意地笑。
瞧啊，瞧啊！雪地上有足迹！
这些是谁留下的？它们会通到哪里去？

[P16] 咕噜牛爸爸正在打呼噜，
呼噜打得震天响。

[P17] 阅读经典图画书
感悟人生大智慧

小老鼠依然聪明 咕噜牛小妞妞也英勇
梅子涵（著名儿童文学作家、教授、儿童文学博士生导师）

你如果读过《咕噜牛》，那么你会记得那只小老鼠的聪明和那只咕噜牛的逃跑。这么多年过去了，咕噜牛竟然就没有想想，那么一只小小的老鼠，哪里有那么大的力量呢？他根本就没有想，而是停留在错误里，还变本加厉夸大记忆、继续恐惧，他这么做，父亲的责任是感动人的，可是一个孩子也就可能因此跟着走进他的错误，结果这错误就接着延续，甚至相传永远。很大的咕噜牛惧怕很小的老鼠，成了不可改变的事儿，成了生命的记忆和特点。人类的世界，这样的荒诞之事实在不少！

咕噜牛小妞妞开始不信，她胆子很大，想去看看明白。风刮得猛，雪下得大，可是她溜出了咕噜牛洞，走到密林中。这是整个故事里最好的精神，是对孩子的成长最有意义的情节，还是个孩子的咕噜牛小妞妞因此看见了各种的动物——其实就是各种的人。

小老鼠依然还是聪明，站到树上借助月光也借助梯子。可是这对小老鼠来说，只不过是智慧的延续和一个新主意的诞生。

咕噜牛小妞妞不一样，她没有听信，是用眼睛直接看见的。月光把站在高高的树上的小老鼠投射到地上，是一个巨大的影子，连尾巴和胡子也巨长，肩上还有巨大的榛子。你要还是孩子的咕噜牛小妞妞不怕，那是不合情理。

可是咕噜牛小妞妞最好不要像她爸爸那样，很多年里不思考、不分析，然后又以和父亲相同的方式描绘给下一代。这就会真的成为生命的记忆、生命的恐惧、生命的习性、生命的相传了。

一个有胆量的人，不等于就是什么都不害怕，永远不逃跑，能够把别人的凶脸描绘和叮嘱搁在一边，亲自去看见和判定，已经是英勇！咕噜牛小妞妞算是英勇的。

我愿意相信，咕噜牛小妞妞不会再重复她爸爸的错误和描绘，我甚至这样想象：咕噜牛和小老鼠，他们的后代，将来成为了非常好的朋友。他们在一起吃饭、喝酒、饮茶，而不是借着吃饭、喝酒、饮茶，把对方吃掉。吃饭、喝酒、饮茶的时候，他们说起前辈间的事，觉得滑稽也有触动，哈哈大笑，陷入沉思。

而真正聪明的我们，现在就已经开始沉思，因为我们是真正聪明的。

阅读经典图画书
透视艺术的幽默趣味

跟着小妞妞的眼睛去冒险
—林佑儒（台湾著名儿童文学作家）

1999年，英国著名儿童文学作家朱莉娅·唐纳森与德国著名插画家阿克塞尔·舍夫勒合作的《咕噜牛》缔造出数百万册的销售佳绩，咕噜牛这只看起来憨厚又可爱的怪物迅速红遍全英国。2004年6月，朱莉娅与阿克塞尔又携手合作推出《咕噜牛小妞妞》，让可爱的怪物咕噜牛再度出场。令人惊喜的是，这次咕噜牛有了一个可爱的小宝宝——小妞妞，她的头顶上刚冒出如嫩笋一般的角，一身浅褐色的毛皮，嘴里尚未长出如咕噜牛爸爸的獠牙，但最重要的是小妞妞和她的爸爸一样，有一双朴实纯真的眼睛。

在这本书中，插画家阿克塞尔使用不透明的压克力颜料来作画，画风清新、色彩鲜艳、构图平稳呈水平式。整本书里特别值得注意的是小妞妞的眼睛，透露出了丰富的表情和内心活动。在寒冬的山洞中，咕噜牛爸爸告诫小妞妞密林深处的危险，父女对望的眼神充满温馨。当咕噜牛爸爸对小妞妞说大老鼠的种种可怕之时，小妞妞的眼神中出现了担心与恐惧。然而，在爸爸沉沉入睡之后，小妞妞却忍不住好奇心和冒险的天性，于是她带着既兴奋又期待的眼神出发了，她想亲自去确认爸爸的话。

你想知道小妞妞是否找到了传说中的那只凶恶的大老鼠吗？建议你快点带着小妞妞的眼睛，一同走入朱莉娅和阿克塞尔所创造出的神秘森林中去冒险吧！

[P1] Julia Donaldson (UK) text  Axel Scheffler (Germany) illustrations
The Gruffalo
Little Gruffalo
Translated by Ren Rongrong
Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press
World Classic Picture Book Series

[P2] Gruffalo's Child
"Gruffalo Dad warned his little girl,
Never go into the deep woods, for there's a fierce big mouse who'll catch you.
But one snowy, windy night,
Little Girl tiptoed out of the house..."
Winds howled, snow fell hard, but Gruffalo's little girl slipped out of her home.
With eyes full of excitement and anticipation, she set off,
She wanted to check her dad's words for herself.
Do you want to know if Little Girl found the legendary fierce big mouse?
I suggest you quickly follow Little Girl,
And step into the mysterious forest to adventure together!
Julia Donaldson (UK) Text  Axel Scheffler (Germany) Illustrations
Ren Rongrong Translator

[P3] Gruffalo Dad warned his little girl,
Never go into the deep woods.
"Why not? Why can't I?"
"Because there's a fierce big mouse who will catch you.
I saw that bad fellow once,
but that was a long, long time ago."

"What does he look like? Tell me, Dad.
Is he very, very fierce, and very, very big?"

[P4] "I can't remember clearly," said Gruffalo Dad.
He thought and thought, scratching his head hard.

"That fierce big mouse is very, very strong,
He has a long, scaly tail, very, very long.

His two eyes are red like two terrible fires,
His whiskers, one by one, are much harder than wire."

[P5] On a snowy, windy night,
Gruffalo Dad was asleep, snoring loudly.
Little Gruffalo was bored at home.
She thought she was brave and bold,
so she tiptoed out of the house.
The wind howled, and the snow fell hard.
Little Gruffalo said, "I'm not afraid!"
She took one step, then another, walking deeper into the forest.

[P6] Look, look! There are tracks in the snow!
Who left them? Where do they lead?
From under the pile of logs, a long tail is sticking out.
Could it be that big mouse?

[P7] That creature slithered out. Its eyes were tiny.
There was no whiskers on its mouth—not even one.

"You're not that big mouse." "Of course not," said the snake,
"He's probably somewhere right now, eating Gruffalo cake."

The wind howled fiercely, and the snow fell heavily.
Little Gruffalo said: "I'm not afraid!"

[P8] Look, look! There are footprints in the snow!
Who left them? Where will they lead?
Two eyes peek out from a tree hollow, shining bright and clear.
Could they be the red eyes of the big mouse?

[P9] That animal flew down. His tail was very short.
He didn't have any whiskers on his mouth—no whiskers at all.

"You're not that big mouse." "Of course not," answered an owl,
"He's probably somewhere right now, eating Gruffalo cake."

The wind was fierce, and the snow fell heavily.
Little Gruffalo said: "I'm not afraid!"

[P10] Look, look! There are footprints in the snow!
Who left these? Where will they lead?
Finally, I see a little mustache! And a home under a tree!
Is this the big mouse's home?

[P11] The animal came out. His eyes weren't like fire, not red at all.
His whiskers weren't hard, and his tail was fluffy.

"You're not that big rat." "Of course not," answered the fox,
"He's probably somewhere right now, eating Gruffalo beef jerky and drinking hot tea."

Little Gruffalo sat on a snow-covered tree stump.
"All lies!" she thought to herself,
"I don't believe there really is a fierce big rat..."

[P12] There's a little mouse over there, just stepping out of his front door.
He's not big, not fierce, but he's still a mouse. Hahaha—
Perfect for my dinner, and it'll taste absolutely delicious!

[P13] "Wait!" said the little mouse, "Before you eat me,
I have a friend you must meet.
As long as I jump onto that hazelnut tree,
I can call him out — a fierce big mouse!"

Little NiuNiu let go after hearing this,
"A fierce big mouse — so it's true!"
"Just wait and see," said the little mouse as he climbed the tree,
shouting loudly for that fierce big mouse.

[P14] The moon came out, round and bright.
A terrifying shadow fell onto the snow.
What kind of animal is this, so big, so fierce, and so strong?
Its tail and whiskers are so long, seeing it makes one's heart tremble!
Its ears are big and long,
and the hazelnut it carries on its shoulder is as big as a boulder!

[P15] "It's that fierce big mouse!" Little Niu Niu screamed as she ran away.
The little mouse jumped down from the tree, giggling with delight.
Look, look! There are footprints in the snow!
Who left these? Where will they lead to?

[P16] Gruffalo Dad is snoring,
His snoring shakes the sky.

[P17] Reading Classic Picture Books
Gaining Great Wisdom in Life

The little mouse is still clever, and Gruffalo's daughter is brave too.
Mei Zihan (Famous children's literature writer, professor, doctoral supervisor of children's literature)

If you've read 'The Gruffalo', you'll remember the cleverness of the little mouse and the Gruffalo's escape. So many years have passed, yet the Gruffalo never thought: how could such a tiny mouse have such great power? He never thought about it, instead staying trapped in his mistake, even exaggerating his memory and continuing his fear. What he did, the father's responsibility, is touching. But a child might also follow him into that mistake, and thus the error continues, even being passed down forever. The big Gruffalo fearing the tiny mouse becomes an unchangeable fact, a memory and characteristic of life. In the human world, such absurdities are not rare!

Gruffalo's daughter initially didn't believe it. She was very brave and wanted to see for herself. The wind was fierce, the snow fell heavily, but she slipped out of the Gruffalo's cave and walked into the dense forest. This is the best spirit in the whole story, the most meaningful part for a child's growth. Still a child, Gruffalo's daughter saw various animals—actually, various kinds of people.

The little mouse is still clever, standing on a tree and using moonlight and a ladder. But for the little mouse, it's just a continuation of wisdom and a new idea.

Gruffalo's daughter is different. She didn't believe the stories; she saw with her own eyes. The moonlight cast the little mouse standing high on the tree onto the ground, creating a huge shadow, with an enormous tail and whiskers, and giant hazelnuts on his shoulder. If a child like Gruffalo's daughter weren't afraid, that would be unreasonable.

But Gruffalo's daughter should not be like her father, who for many years didn't think or analyze, then passed on the same way of description to the next generation. This would truly become a memory of life, a fear of life, a habit of life, a tradition passed down.

A brave person doesn't mean being afraid of nothing, never running away. Being able to put aside others' terrifying descriptions and warnings, and seeing and judging for oneself, is already bravery! Gruffalo's daughter is brave.

I hope to believe that Gruffalo's daughter will not repeat her father's mistakes and descriptions. I even imagine this: the Gruffalo and the little mouse, their descendants, will become very good friends. They will eat, drink wine, and have tea together, not using these to eat each other. When eating, drinking wine, and having tea, they talk about the stories of their ancestors, finding them funny and touching, laughing heartily, and falling into deep thought.

And we, the truly wise, are already beginning to reflect, because we are truly wise.

Reading Classic Picture Books
Perceiving the Humor and Artistry

Following Little Girl's Eyes on an Adventure
—Lin Youru (Famous children's literature writer from Taiwan)

In 1999, British children's literature writer Julia Donaldson and German illustrator Axel Scheffler collaborated on 'The Gruffalo', achieving sales of millions of copies. The Gruffalo, this seemingly clumsy yet adorable monster, quickly became famous across the UK. In June 2004, Julia and Axel collaborated again to release 'The Gruffalo's Child', bringing the beloved monster back. Surprisingly, this time the Gruffalo had a cute baby—Little Girl. She had tiny horns like tender bamboo shoots on her head, light brown fur, and hadn't yet grown the tusks of her Gruffalo father. But most importantly, she had the same pair of honest and pure eyes as her father.

In this book, illustrator Axel used opaque acrylic paints, creating a fresh style, vibrant colors, and balanced, horizontal compositions. The most notable feature throughout the book is Little Girl's eyes, revealing rich expressions and inner emotions. In the cold mountain cave, the Gruffalo father warns Little Girl of the dangers deep in the forest, and their eyes meet with warmth. When the Gruffalo father tells Little Girl about the terrifying big mouse, fear and concern appear in her eyes. However, after her father falls into a deep sleep, Little Girl can't resist her curiosity and adventurous nature. So she sets off with an excited and eager gaze, wanting to personally verify her father's words.

Do you want to know if Little Girl found the legendary fearsome big mouse? I suggest you quickly take Little Girl's eyes and enter the mysterious forest created by Julia and Axel to go on an adventure!
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《咕噜牛小妞妞》的封面，展示了大咕噜牛和小咕噜牛在雪地森林中的温馨场景，背景有雪松和小鸟，左下角有老鼠的石刻画像，右下角有系列标识。
[P2] 本页为绘本《咕噜牛小妞妞》的扉页，左侧文字介绍了故事背景：咕噜牛爸爸警告小妞妞不要去密林，但小妞妞在风雪夜偷偷溜出家门，想亲自验证爸爸的话；右侧是书名和作者信息，配图展示了一只在雪林中警惕前行的小咕噜牛。
[P3] 咕噜牛爸爸警告小妞妞不要去密林，因为那里有只凶恶的大老鼠，小妞妞好奇地询问大老鼠的样子。
[P4] 咕噜牛爸爸努力回忆大老鼠的样子，描述它非常强壮、有带鳞片的长尾巴、红如火焰的眼睛和比铁丝还硬的胡子。
[P5] 在一个风雪交加的夜晚，小妞妞趁爸爸熟睡，偷偷溜出家门，勇敢地向密林深处走去。
[P6] 小妞妞在雪地森林中发现了一串神秘的痕迹，从木头堆下伸出一条长尾巴，她怀疑这可能是大老鼠留下的。
[P7] 小妞妞在风雪中继续前行，发现从木头堆下爬出一条蛇，她以为是大老鼠，但蛇告诉她自己不是，并说大老鼠正在吃咕噜牛蛋糕。小妞妞表示自己并不害怕。
[P8] 小妞妞在雪地森林中发现足迹，并在树洞中看到一双发光的眼睛，怀疑那是大老鼠的红眼睛。
[P9] 小妞妞在风雪中遇到一只猫头鹰，猫头鹰告诉她自己不是大老鼠，并说大老鼠正在吃咕噜牛蛋糕，小妞妞表示自己并不害怕。
[P10] 小妞妞在雪地森林中发现足迹，并看到树下有一个带小胡子的家，怀疑那是大老鼠的住所。
[P11] 小妞妞在雪地森林中遇到一只狐狸，狐狸否认自己是大老鼠，并说大老鼠正在吃咕噜牛肉干喝热茶。小妞妞坐在树墩上，心里怀疑大老鼠的存在，认为大家在骗她。
[P12] 在雪地森林中，一只棕色的怪物正盯着一只刚走出家门的小老鼠，心里盘算着要把它当作夜宵，而旁边还有一个雪人和正在扫雪的小老鼠。
[P13] 在雪地森林中，小老鼠被怪物抓住，他声称自己有个朋友——凶恶的大老鼠，并跳上树去召唤它。小妞妞听后松开手，相信了大老鼠的存在。
[P14] 在月光下的雪地森林里，一个巨大的影子投在雪地上，一只棕色的小动物（小老鼠）被吓得惊恐万分，它描述着影子主人的巨大、凶猛和强壮。
[P15] 小妞妞在雪地森林中惊恐地逃跑，声称遇到了凶恶的大老鼠，而小老鼠则得意地从树上跳下。另一画面中，小老鼠发现雪地上的足迹，好奇地思考着它们的来源和去向。
[P16] 在洞穴中，咕噜牛爸爸正躺在毛皮上熟睡并打呼噜，呼噜声震天响；洞穴外的雪地里，一只小老鼠正沿着足迹前行。
[P17] 本页为绘本《咕噜牛小妞妞》的导读页，包含两位儿童文学作家梅子涵和林佑儒的推荐文字。内容围绕故事主题展开，强调小妞妞勇敢探索、不盲从父辈恐惧的精神，以及绘本的艺术特色和创作背景。
[P18] 画面中，一只棕色的小老鼠正用前爪抓住一根覆盖着积雪的树枝，身体悬空，表情惊恐，似乎在攀爬或躲避危险。
